name.text: Counting Combinations of Toffees, Chestnuts, and Berries

questiontext.text:
In how many ways can a boy select \({@toffee@}\) toffees, \({@chestnut@}\) chestnuts and \({@berries@}\) berries from a jar containing \({@total_toffs@}\) toffees, \({@chestnuts@}\) chestnuts and \({@total_berries@}\) berries.

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

To find the total number of ways to select toffees, chestnuts, and berries together, we multiply these individual counts:

\(^{@total_toffs@}C_{@toffee@} \times {}^{@chestnuts@}C_{@chestnut@} \times {}^{@total_berries@}C_{@berries@}\)

\(^{@total_toffs@}C_{@toffee@}\) represents the number of ways to choose \({@toffee@}\) toffees out of \({@total_toffs@}\) available toffees.

\(^{@chestnuts@}C_{@chestnut@}\) represents the number of ways to choose \({@chestnut@}\) chestnuts out of \({@chestnuts@}\) available chestnuts

\(^{@total_berries@}C_{@berries@}\) represents the number of ways to choose \({@berries@}\) berries out of \({@total_berries@}\) available berries.

Therefore,

\({}^{@total_toffs@}C_{@toffee@} \times {}^{@chestnuts@}C_{@chestnut@} \times {}^{@total_berries@}C_{@berries@}={@ta@}\)
